page: Amazon Web Services r9g.metal-48xl is a bare-metal server positioned in the memory-optimized tier, built on the 64-bit ARM architecture. The host is powered by custom AWS Graviton processors running at a base clock speed of 3.3 GHz. It exposes 192 physical cores with a single thread per core, delivering 192 dedicated hardware execution contexts without hypervisor intervention or shared virtualization overhead.

Memory capacity is configured at 1536.0 GB of RAM, establishing an 8.0 GB per-core allocation ratio that meets the demands of dense in-memory datasets. High-capacity data transit is facilitated by a baseline network bandwidth of 100 Gbps. The chassis does not include local disk storage, necessitating the use of remote network block storage for persistent filesystems, and contains zero discrete GPU accelerators.

The dense core count paired with substantial memory density yields high qualitative efficiency for scale-up architectures, trading GPU acceleration and local drive latency for high-throughput non-virtualized ARM processing. The system requires workloads compiled for arm64 execution. Typical production deployments include large-scale in-memory databases, distributed caching nodes, memory-bound enterprise applications, and real-time big data processing engines.
